intro: Cannavita is on Steinway Street in Astoria, the neighborhood's main shopping strip, and with about 730 products from 105 brands it is the second-largest licensed dispensary we track in Queens' busiest cannabis neighborhood. Pre-rolls lead at around 200 listings, followed by 184 flower options, 158 vapes and 137 edibles, with a 32-item concentrate shelf that is respectable for a shop this size.

MFNY is the deepest brand here with 48 listings, which makes Cannavita one of the better places in Queens to find that label's live resin vapes, tinctures and gummies. Dank By Definition (41) and Zips OG (38) give the flower and pre-roll sections real weight, and Nanticoke, Ayrloom and Fernway round things out. The entry price is among the lowest in the borough: 1906 Boost drops at $3, LEVEL Energy tablets at $3.60 and High Peaks drinks at $4. Terp Bros on Ditmars Boulevard is the other big Astoria shop, slightly larger and more vape-leaning.
know: About 730 products and 105 brands; Astoria's second-largest menu after Terp Bros (800).
Pre-rolls and flower lead (200 and 184), with Dank By Definition and Zips OG the main growers.
The deepest MFNY selection in Queens at 48 listings.
Lowest entry prices in Astoria: micro-dose edibles from $3 and drinks from $4.

faq.q: What is Cannavita best for?
faq.a: Flower and pre-rolls from New York growers, and MFNY products. With nearly 200 pre-rolls, 184 flower options and 48 MFNY listings, it leans toward smokers and live resin fans more than the vape-heavy shops nearby.

faq.q: How far is it from Terp Bros?
faq.a: Cannavita is at 30-30 Steinway Street; Terp Bros is at 36-10 Ditmars Boulevard, roughly a 15-minute walk north. Both are near the N and W line, so comparing the two in one trip is easy.

faq.q: Is there a minimum purchase?
faq.a: Licensed New York dispensaries do not require a minimum spend. Cannavita's cheapest items are single-serve edibles and drinks between $3 and $4, which is a low-risk way to try a product before committing to a multi-pack.

intro: High Tidez is at 1029 Surf Avenue in Coney Island, a few blocks from the boardwalk, with about 720 products from 116 brands. It is a pre-roll shop at heart: just over 250 of its listings are pre-rolls, well ahead of edibles (160), flower (149) and vapes (132). That makes it the better Coney Island option for joints, while Grow Together on Coney Island Avenue is the stronger vape stop.

The brand list is more varied than most shops its size. Honey King leads with 34 listings, followed by STIIIZY, PICC, MFNY, Jaunty and Back Home Cannabis Co., a New York grower. With 116 brands overall it carries more labels than several larger Brooklyn shops. The cheapest items are MFNY live resin gummies at $4.99, LayUp drinks at $5 and High Peaks sparkling lemonade at $5.
know: Pre-roll led: about 252 of 720 products are pre-rolls, the most in the Coney Island area.
Wide brand list for its size at 116 labels, including New York growers like Back Home Cannabis Co.
Vapes are a smaller section (132); Grow Together nearby carries nearly twice as many.
Steps from the Coney Island boardwalk and the Stillwell Avenue subway terminal.

faq.q: What is High Tidez strongest in?
faq.a: Pre-rolls, with about 252 listings, plus a good edible selection of around 160. It is the Coney Island shop to visit for joints and gummies; for vapes, Grow Together on Coney Island Avenue has a deeper wall.

faq.q: Can I smoke on the boardwalk after buying?
faq.a: No. New York bans cannabis smoking wherever tobacco smoking is banned, and the Coney Island boardwalk and beach are smoke-free. Consumption is also prohibited inside the dispensary.

faq.q: How close is it to the subway?
faq.a: The shop is on Surf Avenue a short walk from the Coney Island-Stillwell Avenue terminal, served by the D, F, N and Q lines.

intro: Sunset Cannabis Co is on 55th Street in Sunset Park, the only licensed dispensary we track in the neighborhood, with about 700 products from 72 brands. Pre-rolls are the largest section at just over 210 listings, with flower and vapes tied at 160 each and 137 edibles behind them. For a mid-sized shop it keeps a reasonable 24-item concentrate case.

Hashtag Honey, a New York brand known for infused pre-rolls and flower, is the deepest line here at 43 listings, followed by Ayrloom, Ruby Farms, STIIIZY, Runtz and Revert. The menu's $0.88 floor is a STIIIZY battery, an accessory rather than a product; the real entry price for cannabis is Ayrloom 2:1 drinks at $5.31. Because there is no other licensed shop in Sunset Park, the nearest comparison points are Park Slope to the north and the Coney Island shops to the south.
know: The only licensed dispensary we list in Sunset Park, with about 700 products and 72 brands.
Pre-rolls lead at about 212, with Hashtag Honey (43 listings) the standout brand.
Flower and vapes are evenly matched at roughly 160 each.
The listed $0.88 item is a vape battery; actual cannabis products start at $5.31.

faq.q: Is there another licensed dispensary near Sunset Park?
faq.a: Not in Sunset Park itself. The closest shops we track are Be. and Verdi in Park Slope and Grow Together and High Tidez in Coney Island. Sunset Cannabis Co is the local option for the neighborhood and nearby Bay Ridge.

faq.q: What does Hashtag Honey make?
faq.a: Hashtag Honey is a New York brand focused on infused pre-rolls and flower. With 43 listings it is the deepest line at Sunset Cannabis Co, so this is a good place to see most of its range.

faq.q: Why is the cheapest item under a dollar?
faq.a: That listing is a STIIIZY vape battery, which the shop sells as an accessory. The lowest-priced actual cannabis product at last check was a 10 mg Ayrloom drink at $5.31 before tax.

intro: Stoops NYC is at 182 Fifth Avenue in the Flatiron District, a block from Madison Square Park, and it is the largest of six licensed dispensaries we track across Chelsea and Flatiron with about 690 products from 111 brands. Pre-rolls (217) and vapes (206) are the two big sections, with 152 edibles and a smaller 90-item flower selection, plus 20 concentrates.

Jaunty and Florist Farms are the deepest brands here with 32 listings apiece, covering all-in-one vapes and New York-grown pre-rolls respectively, and Select, Cannabals, Bonanza Cannabis and PAX fill in the vape and pod options. Stoops also has one of the lowest entry prices in Manhattan: Ayrloom 1:1 drinks at $3.39 and Jaunty hash-infused gummy two-packs at $4.52. For flower, The Alchemy on 8th Avenue and Gotham on 10th Avenue are the nearby alternatives, though none of the Chelsea shops goes especially deep on it.
know: Largest menu in Chelsea and Flatiron: about 690 products and 111 brands.
Pre-rolls and vapes lead at over 200 each; flower is lighter at about 90.
Jaunty and Florist Farms (32 listings each) are the main lines; PAX pods are stocked.
Among the lowest entry prices in Manhattan, with infused drinks from $3.39.

faq.q: Which Chelsea or Flatiron dispensary has the most selection?
faq.a: Stoops NYC, with about 690 products. The Alchemy (541), Poppin (506) and Gotham Chelsea (501) are next, followed by Bud & Honey (418) and Verdi (351). Between the six, the area has roughly 3,000 products, the second-largest neighborhood total in our data after Midtown.

faq.q: Is Stoops a good place for flower?
faq.a: It is adequate rather than deep, with about 90 flower listings. The shop is strongest in pre-rolls and vapes. If flower is the priority, the Chelsea cluster overall is light on it; the Upper West Side or East Village shops carry more.

faq.q: What is the closest subway?
faq.a: The 23rd Street stations on the N, R, W and the 6 are each about two blocks away, and the shop is a short walk from Madison Square Park.

intro: The Travel Agency's SoHo store is at 598 Broadway, just below Houston Street, and it is the largest of the four licensed dispensaries we track in SoHo with about 660 products from 65 brands. Unusually for a Manhattan shop, edibles are the biggest category at 175 listings, followed by vapes (166), flower (139) and pre-rolls (133). It also carries one of the larger topical selections in the city at 10 items, plus 13 tinctures.

RYTHM, a multi-state flower and vape brand, has 69 listings here, more than at almost any other shop in our data, and Select, Heavy Hitters, Ruby Farms, Grassroots and Find. complete a brand list that skews toward established names. The Travel Agency also runs stores at Union Square and in Downtown Brooklyn with a similar mix. The cheapest items are TUNE infused seltzers and Ayrloom drinks at $5.
know: Largest SoHo menu: about 660 products and 65 brands; Alta (427) and The Flowery SoHo (298) are the next largest.
Edible-led (175), with the deepest RYTHM selection in our data (69 listings).
Better than most shops for topicals (10) and tinctures (13).
Part of The Travel Agency group, which also has Union Square and Downtown Brooklyn locations.

faq.q: What sets The Travel Agency SoHo apart from the other SoHo shops?
faq.a: Selection size and an edibles-first shelf. It has about 660 products to Alta's 427, and the largest RYTHM lineup we track. Alta leans toward edibles and topicals as well, while The Flowery SoHo and Dagmar on West Broadway are smaller and more pre-roll focused.

faq.q: Does it carry topicals and tinctures?
faq.a: Yes, and more than most. At last check it listed 10 topicals and 13 tinctures, which puts it among the better Manhattan shops for non-inhalable products alongside Alta a few blocks away.

faq.q: Is this the same as The Travel Agency in Union Square?
faq.a: Same group, different store. The Union Square location is at 835 Broadway and carries about 580 products with a similar brand mix; the Downtown Brooklyn store on Flatbush Avenue is the third.

intro: Weedside is at 50-50 72nd Street in Woodside, Queens, the only licensed dispensary we track in the neighborhood, with about 660 products from 99 brands. Pre-rolls (200) and vapes (191) are the two main sections, with 123 flower options and 117 edibles behind them and a 22-item concentrate shelf.

Hashtag Honey is far and away the deepest brand here at 61 listings, the most of that label at any shop in our data, so Weedside is the place to see its full infused pre-roll and flower range. MFNY (43), Ayrloom, Ruby Farms, Jaunty and Rove cover vapes, drinks and more pre-rolls. Ignore the $2.26 floor on the menu, which is bottled water; cannabis products start at 1906 Sleep drops for $4.52 and TUNE seltzers at $5.65. The Jackson Heights shops, Purple Buds and ENFLOR, are the nearest alternatives along the 7 line.
know: Woodside's only licensed dispensary in our data, with about 660 products and 99 brands.
The deepest Hashtag Honey selection anywhere we track, at 61 listings.
Pre-rolls and vapes lead at around 200 each; flower is about 123.
Near the 69th and 74th Street stops on the 7 line; Jackson Heights shops are two stops east.

faq.q: What is Weedside known for?
faq.a: Hashtag Honey. With 61 listings it carries more of that New York brand's infused pre-rolls and flower than any other shop we track, backed by a strong MFNY selection for live resin vapes and gummies.

faq.q: Is there a dispensary closer to Woodside than Jackson Heights?
faq.a: Weedside is the only licensed shop we list in Woodside. Purple Buds and ENFLOR in Jackson Heights are the nearest alternatives, both reachable on the 7 train, and Astoria's shops are a short bus or train ride north.

faq.q: Why is the cheapest listing $2.26?
faq.a: That item is a bottle of Poland Spring water, which the shop sells alongside cannabis. The lowest-priced cannabis product at last check was a two-pack of 1906 Sleep drops at $4.52 before tax.

intro: CONBUD is at 85 Delancey Street on the Lower East Side, with about 590 products from 92 brands, the larger of the two licensed dispensaries we track in the Chinatown and LES area. Pre-rolls are its biggest section by a wide margin at around 210 listings, followed by 138 edibles, 128 vapes and 86 flower options. It also lists nine topicals, more than most downtown shops.

Ruby Farms, a New York pre-roll and flower grower, leads the shelf with 40 listings, and Claybourne Co., Ayrloom, Mfused, Zips and Wizard Trees cover pre-rolls, drinks, edibles and flower. The lowest-priced listing is a $3 lighter; the entry price for cannabis is LEVEL tablet two-packs at $4. Mighty Lucky on the Bowery is the other licensed shop nearby, with a more edible-heavy menu of about 540 products.
know: Largest menu in Chinatown and the LES: about 590 products and 92 brands, versus 540 at Mighty Lucky.
Pre-roll led, with about 210 listings and Ruby Farms the deepest line.
Nine topicals listed, a better selection than most downtown shops.
Cannabis prices start at $4 for LEVEL tablets; the $3 listing is a lighter.

faq.q: CONBUD or Mighty Lucky — which should I visit?
faq.a: CONBUD for pre-rolls and flower; it has about 210 pre-rolls to Mighty Lucky's 133 and nearly 90 flower options. Mighty Lucky is the stronger edible and tincture stop. They are a few blocks apart on Delancey and the Bowery, so visiting both is easy.

faq.q: Which New York brands does CONBUD carry?
faq.a: Ruby Farms is the deepest at 40 listings, and Claybourne Co., Ayrloom, Zips and Wizard Trees are all stocked. That gives the shop a strong local pre-roll and flower selection.

faq.q: How do I get there?
faq.a: CONBUD is at 85 Delancey Street, about a block from the Delancey Street-Essex Street station on the F, J, M and Z lines.

intro: Milligrams is on Greenpoint Avenue in Greenpoint, the only licensed dispensary we track in the neighborhood, with about 590 products from 87 brands. Pre-rolls lead at around 173 listings, with vapes (138), edibles (133) and flower (120) close behind, plus a dozen concentrates and a handful of tinctures and topicals.

Ruby Farms is the deepest brand at 41 listings, giving the shop a strong New York pre-roll section, and Heavy Hitters, MFNY, Ayrloom, Fernway and Camino cover vapes, live resin, drinks and gummies. The entry price is $3.50 for an Ayrloom 1:1 Honeycrisp drink, with other Ayrloom beverages at $5. Williamsburg's six licensed shops are the nearest alternatives, a short ride south on the G or a walk down Manhattan Avenue.
know: Greenpoint's only licensed dispensary in our data, with about 590 products and 87 brands.
Evenly spread across pre-rolls, vapes, edibles and flower (120 to 173 each).
Ruby Farms (41 listings) is the main pre-roll line; Fernway and Camino add vapes and gummies.
Entry price of $3.50 for a 5 mg infused drink; six Williamsburg shops are within a short trip.

faq.q: Is Milligrams the only dispensary in Greenpoint?
faq.a: It is the only licensed one we track in the neighborhood. The next-closest options are the Williamsburg shops, including Gotham Domino and The Flowery Brooklyn, which are a short G train ride or a walk south.

faq.q: What is Milligrams good for?
faq.a: A balanced basket. Its four main categories are all between 120 and 173 listings, so it covers pre-rolls, vapes, edibles and flower without a glaring gap, and Ruby Farms gives it a solid New York pre-roll selection.

faq.q: What is the nearest subway?
faq.a: The Greenpoint Avenue station on the G line is steps from the shop at 58 Greenpoint Avenue.

intro: The Travel Agency's Union Square store is at 835 Broadway near 13th Street, with about 580 products from 61 brands, the largest of three licensed dispensaries we track around Gramercy and Union Square. The menu is evenly built, with vapes (152), pre-rolls (146) and edibles (137) within a few listings of each other, about 100 flower options and a 26-item concentrate shelf.

RYTHM is the deepest brand here at 55 listings, with Select, Heavy Hitters, Ruby Farms, Grassroots and MFNY behind it, the same established-brand mix found at the group's SoHo and Downtown Brooklyn stores. The cheapest items are Harney Brothers coffee shots, Ayrloom drinks and TUNE seltzers at $5. Green Genius on 3rd Avenue, a few blocks east, carries more brands and a deeper vape wall; Smiley Exotics on East 30th Street is the smaller third option.
know: Largest menu in the Gramercy and Union Square area: about 580 products and 61 brands.
Evenly split across vapes, pre-rolls and edibles at roughly 140 to 150 each.
RYTHM (55 listings) leads, with Select and Heavy Hitters next.
Part of The Travel Agency group with SoHo and Downtown Brooklyn stores; steps from Union Square station.

faq.q: How does this compare to Green Genius nearby?
faq.a: The Travel Agency Union Square has slightly more products (about 580 to 549) and a more balanced shelf. Green Genius lists more brands (107 to 61) and leans toward vapes and edibles with very few pre-rolls. Pick The Travel Agency for pre-rolls, Green Genius for vape variety.

faq.q: What brands does it carry the most of?
faq.a: RYTHM with 55 listings, then Select (45), Heavy Hitters (39), Ruby Farms (36), Grassroots (26) and MFNY (19). It is a good stop for comparing several national flower and vape brands in one place.

faq.q: Can I order ahead for pickup?
faq.a: The store's menu is published online, which is where Sensei's prices come from, and The Travel Agency's stores take online orders for in-store pickup. Confirm current options on the shop's own menu page.

intro: The Travel Agency's Downtown Brooklyn store is at 122 Flatbush Avenue, near the Barclays Center and the Atlantic Avenue transit hub, with about 560 products from 57 brands. It is the largest of the four licensed dispensaries we track in the Brooklyn Heights and Downtown area, and like its SoHo sibling it is edible-led: 164 edible listings, then 142 vapes, 124 pre-rolls and 88 flower options, plus a better-than-average 10 topicals and 12 tinctures.

RYTHM, Heavy Hitters, Ruby Farms and Select each have 44 to 47 listings, an unusually even top tier that makes this a good place to compare those four brands directly, with Grassroots and Camino behind them. The cheapest items are Ayrloom drinks, TUNE seltzers and Minny Grown cocktail-style drinks at $5. Buzzy NY on Court Street and The Garden Club on Smith Street are the nearby alternatives, both smaller.
know: Largest menu in Brooklyn Heights and Downtown Brooklyn: about 560 products and 57 brands.
Edible-led (164), with topicals (10) and tinctures (12) better stocked than most Brooklyn shops.
Four brands tied at the top: RYTHM, Heavy Hitters, Ruby Farms and Select, each around 45 listings.
Steps from Atlantic Avenue-Barclays Center, the busiest subway hub in Brooklyn.

faq.q: Which Downtown Brooklyn dispensary has the most selection?
faq.a: The Travel Agency on Flatbush Avenue, with about 560 products. Buzzy NY on Court Street has roughly 380 and The Garden Club on Smith Street about 210. Buzzy is worth a look for its wider brand list of 79 labels.

faq.q: Is it a good place for edibles?
faq.a: Yes, edibles are its largest category at about 164 listings, including Camino and Wyld gummies, and it carries more topicals and tinctures than most Brooklyn shops.

faq.q: How do I get there by subway?
faq.a: The store is a short walk from Atlantic Avenue-Barclays Center, served by the 2, 3, 4, 5, B, D, N, Q and R lines, as well as the LIRR.
